title: Site rules: approved products, plug-in equipment and reporting
audience: Cleaners in any cleaning-group business who use products, plug-in machines or report site incidents.
learningOutcomes: Identify which products and equipment are approved for a job before opening or using them.
Move a plug-in machine to another socket using the switch-off sequence.
Report a defective machine, a hazard or an accident to the supervisor without delay, without attempting an electrical repair.
Explain why a machine is never lifted or dragged by its cord.

instruction.heading: Use only what the business has approved
instruction.body: Every product and machine used on a job should come from the list your business has approved. A product brought from home, an unlabelled bottle or a borrowed machine may not match the safety data, the dilution rules or the equipment checks that the business relies on. If you find a product you did not expect, do not use it and do not pour it into another container. Tell the supervisor, who will confirm whether it is approved. Your business records its approved list in the job or site record, so check there before you open any container.

instruction.heading: Plug-in equipment and the safe way to move a plug
instruction.body: Electrical hazards are a main risk with cleaning machines in occupied buildings. Vacuums, scrubbers and extractors have cords that can be damaged, that can trip people, and that can be drawn into water. When a machine must move to another socket, switch the machine off at the machine, switch the wall socket off, and only then remove the plug. Take hold of the plug body, not the cord. Move the machine by its body or handle, never by its lead. The site rule is also that you do not unplug any plug on site unless you have been directed to handle it. Ask first when the plug belongs to the client, the building or another contractor.

instruction.heading: Defective equipment and electrical repair
instruction.body: If a cord is cut, a plug is cracked or warm, a switch sticks or a machine smells of burning, stop using it at once. Set the machine aside and label it as defective in the way your business directs. Tell your manager straight away. Electrical equipment is never repaired by the worker, even for a small fault such as a loose plug or a cut cord that could be taped. Repairs are arranged by the business through a suitably qualified person. Confirm them with the business before relying on any testing record.

instruction.heading: Misuse, hazards and reporting
instruction.body: Tampering with the equipment or materials you were given is misuse, whether it happens on purpose or through carelessness. Removing a guard, bypassing a safety switch, using a machine for a task it was not built for, or mixing products to get a stronger result all count as misuse. Your duty to report extends to every hazard you notice while working, not only to equipment faults. Report it to your manager immediately. The business then assesses the hazard and decides how to remove or reduce the risk. Do not decide alone that a hazard is too small to mention. Report every accident, however minor, and report near misses too, because a slip you recovered from shows where a control needs to change.

instruction.heading: Personal protective equipment before the first task
instruction.body: Wear the personal protective equipment that the job sheet lists for every task, not only when you expect to be close to a chemical. Check the PPE before you start. Gloves with tears or holes, or eye protection that is scratched or fogged, do not protect you and should be replaced before you begin.

procedure: Check the job record for the approved product list and the required PPE before opening any container.
Confirm each machine passed its start-of-job check, using the business's inspection checklist.
Before moving a plug-in machine to another socket, switch off the machine, switch off the socket, then remove the plug at the plug body.
Keep cords out of walkways and away from water. Never move a machine by its lead.
Stop using any defective equipment, set it aside, label it and report it to your manager without delay.
Report any accident, near miss or hazard to your manager straight away and record it as the incident procedure requires.

workedExamples.situation: You are vacuuming an office and the cord of your vacuum is cut close to the plug. A colleague suggests a strip of tape will hold it. The client is waiting.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do, and what do you tell the client?
workedExamples.reasoning: Switch off the machine at the machine, switch off the socket, then remove the plug at the plug body. Do not tape or repair the cord. Set the vacuum aside, label it defective and report it to your manager. Tell the client's contact that the machine is out of service and that the job will continue with an approved spare or be rescheduled, as the business directs.

workedExamples.situation: A wet-floor sign has blown over, and a scrubber's cord is lying across a doorway where a visitor is walking.
workedExamples.reasoning: Make the doorway safe first. Stop the machine and move the cord out of the walkway, then set the sign back up. Report the near miss and the cord position to the supervisor so that the route can be planned differently on the next job.

workedExamples.situation: While setting up, you notice a loose tile edge on the entry step. Repairing tiles is not part of your job.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you report it, and do you fix it?
workedExamples.reasoning: Report it to your manager immediately, and mark or guard the step with a sign if you can do so safely. Do not attempt the repair yourself. The business assesses the hazard and decides what happens next.

equipmentAndPpe: Gloves suited to the product in use, in good condition
Eye protection where splashing is possible
The job sheet or site record listing approved products and required PPE
Defective-equipment label or tag, as the business sets
Incident or hazard report form, as the business sets

commonErrors.error: Using a product brought from home because it seemed to work well.
commonErrors.prevention: Use only approved products. Report any unknown product to the supervisor and wait for a decision.

commonErrors.error: Moving a machine by its cord, or unplugging it by pulling the cord.
commonErrors.prevention: Move the machine by its body. Switch off the machine and the socket, then remove the plug at the plug body.

commonErrors.error: Taping a damaged cord and carrying on with the job.
commonErrors.prevention: Set the machine aside and report it. Do not repair electrical equipment.

commonErrors.error: Leaving a minor slip or a small hazard unreported because it seems unimportant.
commonErrors.prevention: Report every accident, near miss and hazard to your manager without delay.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: They vary by state and territory and by workplace. Confirm them before relying on this lesson for compliance.
This lesson does not authorise anyone to repair, test or certify electrical equipment. Repair is arranged by the business through a suitably qualified person.
The business's own incident procedure applies until they are confirmed.
Chemical handling follows the product label and the safety data sheet, which the business must keep available at the site.

qualityStandard: Products used on the job match the approved list in the job record.
Every plug-in machine moved between sockets is switched off at the machine and at the socket before the plug is removed.
No defective equipment is used. Each fault is set aside, labelled and reported to the manager.
Each accident, near miss or hazard seen during the job is reported without delay.
documentationEvidence: Start-of-job equipment check record, showing each machine was in working order.
Hazard, near-miss or accident report showing time, location and the manager notified.
Record of any unapproved product found and the supervisor's decision about it.
summary: Use only approved products and equipment.
Switch off the machine and the socket before moving a plug, and never move a machine by its cord.
Stop using defective equipment and do not repair it yourself.
Report accidents, near misses and hazards to your manager without delay.

knowledgeChecks.question: You find a cleaning product in a cupboard that is not on the approved list. What do you do?
options: Use it if the label looks safe and the dilution seems right to you today
Do not use it, and tell the supervisor so they can confirm whether it is approved
Decant it into an approved bottle and label the bottle with the product name

knowledgeChecks.question: A vacuum must be moved to a different socket. What is the correct order?
options: Remove the plug by pulling the cord, then switch off the machine
Remove the plug at the cord while the machine is still switched on
Switch off the machine, switch off the socket, then remove the plug at the plug body

knowledgeChecks.question: The cord of a machine is damaged. Which action is correct?
options: Wrap it with tape and keep working if the machine still runs and check it again after the next room
Set the machine aside, label it, and report it to your manager without attempting a repair
Use it carefully for the rest of the day and report it at the end of the week
